children: shares slid 6.88% to $145.98 at 9:55 a.m. ET on November 16 in regular trading, among the hardest-hit AI chip names. The Next Web, summarizing a Wall Street Journal report, said Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to rein in the company's financing of the AI industry after a stretch of aggressive computing deals and startup investments. A UBS estimate cited in the report put the potential market impact at $50 billion or more.

Marvell is tied to Nvidia on several fronts. Nvidia invested $2 billion in Marvell in March 2026 and is a major holder of Lumentum too, TechCrunch reported when Marvell announced its takeover. That deal, an all-stock exchange of 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share, valued Lumentum at about $1,132 per share and promised more than $1 billion in annual run-rate cost synergies, with closing expected in the first half of 2028.

The announcement price implied Marvell at about $252 a share; at $145.98, Marvell is down roughly 42% since then, so its acquisition currency has shrunk sharply. GuruFocus gives Marvell a GF Score of 84/100, with growth and momentum offsetting weaker profitability. Shares trade about 13% above the $128.64 GF Value, a modestly overvalued reading even after the slide. That leaves limited valuation support if AI financing tightens. The next hurdle is Marvell's fiscal third-quarter report in early December, where custom silicon guidance will show how much Nvidia-linked demand still holds.

title: Marvell Stocks Slide 6.88% as Nvidia Financing Pullback Report Hits AI Connectivity Bet
